title: Stalker uses husband's name to lure teacher, stabs her 20 times in Faridabad
content: In a harrowing incident in Faridabad, a young teacher was brutally murdered by a stalker who deceived her into meeting him at the school gate by using her husband's name. The attacker stabbed her repeatedly, exceeding twenty times, in front of both students and staff. Authorities apprehended the 21-year-old assailant within hours. The victim, a mother of two, had previously warned the stalker about impending legal action.

title: 'Being hounded despite apology’: Noida teen in PM abuse FIR forced to change homes
content: A Noida teenager and her mother have moved homes three times after an FIR was filed. The FIR, based on a video, names the 15-year-old for alleged profanities. She has since apologized and is receiving threats on social media. Police personnel and strangers visited their residence, causing safety concerns for the family. The family has moved to an undisclosed location due to ongoing threats.

title: CWG para champions complain against IOA staff, seek action over 'misconduct'
content: After the recent success of Dilip Gavit and Mohammed Basil, Indian para athletes and coaches have come forward with formal complaints against a member of the IOA media committee. The allegations detail instances of rude behaviour directed at the para athletes, leading to a heated confrontation that spiraled into a brief physical clash. The athletes are calling for the IOA to take action regarding the official's conduct during the Games.

title: Oil rebounds from three-week low as Hormuz tensions keep supply fears alive
content: Oil prices saw a modest recovery on Tuesday after a significant decline. Benchmark Brent crude climbed to $84.26 and WTI crude reached $80.75. This rebound followed a sharp slide after US President Donald Trump paused military action against Iran. Shipping patterns are changing, and concerns about energy supply risks persist. Oil prices remain below their earlier peak of $126 per barrel.

title: OpenAI models hacked Hugging Face; CEO warns America on Chinese AI
content: China's open-weight AI models are rapidly advancing, potentially surpassing American developers soon. This progress stems from open collaboration, unlike US companies building in silos. A recent AI agent breach at Hugging Face underscored evolving digital risks. Hugging Face used a Chinese open-weight model to resolve the security incident. AI cybersecurity is predicted to become a massive global market driven by open-source models.

title: ‘Who approved it?’: HI president Dilip Tirkey seeks answers on jersey switch
content: Hockey India president Dilip Tirkey questions the director general's authority.  He seeks accountability and transparency in the recent jersey colour change.  Tirkey expressed surprise at learning about the redesign through social media.  He emphasised the need for governance and consultation for symbolic decisions.  The president requested a comprehensive reply with documentary evidence by Tuesday.

title: SC expands ambit of Sec 498A to cover cruelty in live-ins too
content: The Supreme Court has extended legal protection to live-in relationships.  These relationships are now covered under Section 498A of the IPC.  The court stated that the law must adapt to changing societal norms.  Cruelty within such relationships will now be punishable by law.  This decision aims to protect women from domestic violence and harassment.

title: 'Forever grateful': Dilip bids emotional farewell after 5 years with Team India
content: T Dilip concluded his five-year tenure as India's fielding coach with a heartfelt farewell message. He significantly transformed the team's fielding culture during his impactful service. The innovative fielding medal ceremony became a memorable dressing-room tradition during his tenure. Dilip cherished being part of numerous team triumphs across various formats.

title: Lauren Sanchez worked at waterpark; 40 years later, she takes luxurious ocean trips
content: Lauren Sanchez's career evolved from a teenage waterpark job to ocean conservation leadership. She recently explored the Galápagos Islands, highlighting shark importance. The Bezos Earth Fund supports significant marine conservation projects in the region. These initiatives protect vast ocean areas and numerous marine species. Sanchez's work now focuses on protecting vital ocean ecosystems.

title: Census phase 2 to begin Aug 17, will capture caste, parents’ birth details
content: The Census 2027 population enumeration phase begins August 17 in snow-bound northern areas. This phase will capture caste details for the first time since 1931. Parents' date and birthplace will also be recorded as declared by respondents. Passport and Aadhaar numbers may be collected voluntarily during the exercise. The questionnaire for this significant census phase will be notified soon.

title: Africa plans $50bn Congo water diversion to revive shrinking Lake Chad
content: Lake Chad's dramatic shrinkage has brought about severe impacts on the lives of millions. To counteract this crisis, governments are investing in initiatives aimed at rehabilitating the lake's ecosystem. A noteworthy solution includes the ambitious Transaqua project, which seeks to channel water from the Congo River back into Lake Chad. This vital endeavor aims not only to replenish the lake but also to foster economic growth in the surrounding regions.

title: Australian grandfather, 82, and grandson cycle 5,300km for MND
content: An 82-year-old grandfather and his 18-year-old grandson completed a nearly 5,300-kilometre cycling journey across Australia after riding for six weeks from Broome to Bowral. The pair undertook the challenge to raise money and awareness for motor neurone disease, inspired by a family member who died from the condition.

title: Nvidia CEO predicts these jobs will pay 6 figures as data centers boom
content: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang predicts a bright future for skilled tradespeople.  AI data center expansion drives significant infrastructure build-out globally.  This growth will create many six-figure jobs for electricians and construction workers.  Demand for electricians is particularly high for building AI facilities.  Other tech leaders also warn of labor shortages impacting manufacturing and construction.

title: Bankipur bypoll: PK adds a dash of yellow to Bihar palette of saffron & green
content: Prashant Kishor secured his first electoral victory in the Bankipur bypoll. This win challenges the established green and saffron political dominance in Bihar. Kishor, a renowned political strategist, launched his Jan Suraaj Party after extensive grassroots work. His victory sends a message to national parties regarding key issues. The outcome suggests Bihar may accommodate a third political force.

title: Shoulder surgery, 7 months out, one throw: How Yash Vir Singh won CWG bronze
content: Yash Vir Singh arrived in Glasgow with little attention but left with a Commonwealth Games bronze after a personal-best final throw. In this interview with TimesofIndia.com, he opens up about the injury that nearly derailed his career, the months spent in rehabilitation, Neeraj Chopra's words before his medal-winning attempt and the father who has guided him since his first throws with a bamboo javelin.

title: Jantar Mantar not okay for protests? SC seeks replies
content: The Supreme Court has asked the Centre and Delhi authorities for their responses.  A PIL seeks designated protest sites, citing Jantar Mantar's lack of amenities.  The court noted Jantar Mantar's unsuitability for holding protests and basic facilities.  Petitioner mentioned potential marches and police actions to prevent violence.  Authorities are responsible for handling emerging situations and ensuring law takes its course.

title: Here's how Michael Phelps built his $100 million fortune in 2026
content: Michael Phelps turned his legendary Olympic achievements into a multi-million dollar empire. By securing high-value endorsements from renowned brands post-retirement, he also channeled his success into impactful ventures. His establishment of a foundation showcases his commitment to youth education in swimming and healthy living. Additionally, Phelps's investment in the mental health platform shows his suppport for emotional wellness.

title: Josh Allen’s family stood by him through rejection, injuries and NFL success
content: The story of Josh Allen illustrates how unwavering support from family and relentless hard work paved his way to NFL greatness. Despite rejections and early criticism, he learned the value of consistency from his father's example. Overcoming injuries and playoff disappointments, Allen's journey reveals that the heart of success often beats stronger in the shadows, driven by family faith.

title: How LeBron James turned childhood pain into a $41M education mission
content: LeBron James established a scholarship program for Akron students.  This initiative helps approximately eleven hundred students attend college.  The program stems from his own childhood struggles with financial instability.  He never attended college himself, entering the NBA directly after high school.  This mission provides a realistic chance for education beyond high school.

title: UFC fighter Allan Nascimento dies aged 34 after apparent heart attack
content: UFC flyweight Allan Nascimento has died at the age of 34, just weeks after his most recent fight. The promotion confirmed he suffered a medical emergency and shared details in an official statement. A Brazilian Jiu Jitsu black belt, Nascimento compiled a 22-7 professional record and earned respect for his submission skills. Tributes have poured in from fellow UFC stars, including Dustin Poirier, Henry Cejudo and Mackenzie Dern.

title: Bangladesh seeks India’s stand on Sheikh Hasina’s Aug 5 virtual address
content: Bangladesh seeks India's clarification on supporting Sheikh Hasina's upcoming virtual address.  Dhaka wants assurances that Indian territory will not be used for political statements.  The government fears such activities could destabilize Bangladesh and harm bilateral ties.  India has previously indicated it does not expect fugitives to make political statements.  No decision has been made regarding Prime Minister Tarique Rahman's attendance at the BRICS Summit.

title: Monsoon Session: Opposition toughens stand, washout likely
content: Parliament's monsoon session faces potential washout amid opposition demands. Opposition insists on discussing Ram temple donations and police actions. Union ministers criticize opposition for boycotting legislative proceedings. Bills were passed without debate due to the ongoing parliamentary standoff. The government has not yet assured discussions on the opposition's key demands.

title: India crosses 20k organ transplants/yr for 1st time
content: India performed a record 20,138 organ transplants in 2025, a significant increase over previous years. Delhi-NCR led the nation in transplant procedures, while Tamil Nadu topped deceased organ donors. India now ranks third globally in total organ transplants, after the US and China. Deceased donor transplants continue to fall short of the substantial demand for organs. Government initiatives aim to strengthen organ donation and transplant services across the country.

title: Brij Bhushan acquitted in sexual harassment case
content: A Delhi court has acquitted former WFI chief Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh.  The sexual harassment case involved allegations from several women wrestlers.  Suspended WFI assistant secretary Vinod Tomar was also found not guilty.  The trial concluded after three years with the court examining many witnesses.  This verdict follows months of protests by prominent wrestlers demanding justice.

title: Vijay's Jana Nayagan crosses Rs 300 crore worldwide on Day 12
content: Jana Nayagan continues to perform well at the box office, earning over Rs 3.85 crore on its twelfth day. The film has achieved a total India gross collection of Rs 209.35 crore and Rs 179.45 crore net. Overseas collections have also been strong, contributing Rs 1 crore on day twelve. This brings the worldwide gross collection for Jana Nayagan to Rs 301.35 crore. The political action drama saw a 28.

title: J&K: Days after Kulgam terror attack, man with grenade held in Pulwama
content: A suspect was apprehended in Pulwama carrying a hand grenade and anti-national posters. This arrest occurred during a security operation following recent migrant worker killings. Authorities booked the local man under stringent anti-terror laws, including the UAPA. Security forces are increasing patrols and checkpoints across the valley. This intensified security aims to maintain peace and prevent further unlawful activities.

title: Lower min age for MD, directors to 18: Parliamentary panel
content: A parliamentary panel suggests lowering the minimum director age to eighteen years.  The committee also backs raising the maximum director age to seventy-five years.  Special NCLT benches for insolvency matters are recommended for efficient asset resolution.  The panel proposes retaining the ten crore net profit threshold for CSR applicability.  New provisions will enable seamless re-domiciliation of foreign companies to IFSC.

title: Withdraw cases, allow youngsters to continue studies: SC to states
content: The Supreme Court permitted governments to withdraw cases against student protesters.  This move aims to allow students to pursue their studies without prosecution fears.  However, cases against individuals with criminal records will not be dropped.  The court will also establish guidelines for the use of graded force by police.  Discussions on modalities for dropping cases against genuine students are ongoing.

title: Government to sell up to 6.5% stake in LIC, may mop up Rs 31k cr
content: The government is selling up to 6.5% of LIC shares through an offer for sale. This divestment aims to meet minimum public shareholding norms ahead of schedule. The offer begins Tuesday and closes Wednesday with a base price of Rs 382. Successful sale will raise approximately Rs 31,400 crore for the government. This move contributes significantly to the government's annual disinvestment target.

title: 21 Bangladesh nationals detained in J&K’s Ramban
content: Twenty-one Bangladesh nationals were detained in Ramban district last week.  Officials are questioning them to learn who facilitated their movement.  The group was caught moving in two vehicles during a checking drive.  None of them could produce valid identity or travel documents.  Investigators are probing if any network assisted these illegal immigrants.

title: Foreign, private banks raise over 68% FCNR(B) funds
content: Foreign currency deposits saw a significant increase between June and July.  Banks aggressively mobilized these funds, taking advantage of RBI incentives.  HSBC, SBI, and ICICI Bank led the collection efforts for these deposits.  Foreign banks showed the fastest proportional growth in their deposit holdings.  Overall, the mobilization was concentrated among the top ten banking institutions.

title: 'Flavouring neutral alcohol isn't right in spirit'
content: The FSSAI has prohibited adding rum or whisky flavour to spirits. This practice misrepresents the true nature of alcoholic beverages and misleads consumers. Manufacturers were found using neutral alcohol and adding identical flavouring substances. Several companies, including United Spirits, faced prohibitions and notices. The regulator stressed that characteristic taste should develop naturally through base ingredients.

title: ARAI's study on E20 fuel impact may be made public
content: Government agencies are considering releasing the ARAI study on E20 fuel's impact.  This report, submitted in June 2024, studied E10-compatible vehicles.  Fuel consumption increased slightly for two-wheelers and cars in the study.  Mass emissions met regulatory requirements for all vehicles tested.  The release aims to remove misconceptions among vehicle users about E20 fuel.

title: UPS has attracted just 4% of NPS subscribers: Government
content: The Unified Pension Scheme for central government employees has seen low adoption rates.  Only a small percentage of National Pension Trust subscribers have opted for this new scheme.  The government introduced UPS with assured pension benefits and gratuity provisions.  However, the response has been tepid, prompting an extension of the migration deadline.  No changes are currently being considered to replace the Unified Pension Scheme.

title: SC: How can transgender ID cards be rendered invalid?
content: The Supreme Court has sought the government's response regarding the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Amendment Act.  Concerns were raised that the new law might erase existing benefits for transgender individuals.  Senior advocates reported that hormone treatment is being denied due to fear of prosecution.  They also alleged the discontinuation of the national portal for transgenders.  The court questioned the retrospective invalidation of previously issued transgender identity cards.

title: A seat for JSP's 'school bag': Why Kishor's Bankipur win is a warning for BJP, RJD
content: Prashant Kishor achieved a remarkable victory in the Bankipur byelection, effectively breaking the BJP's three-decade dominance on the assembly seat. This triumph represents Kishor's resurgence in politics following his party's prior electoral drubbing in the state. He leveraged this win to critique Bihar's chief minister and emphasize the need for development. The outcome comes as an embarrassment for the current government's leadership.

title: India-origin cricketer Reddy handed 8-year ban by ICC for corruption
content: USA cricketer Bodugum Akhilesh Reddy has been banned from all cricket for eight years after an ICC tribunal found him guilty of three Anti-Corruption Code breaches linked to the 2025 Abu Dhabi T10. He was found to have attempted match-fixing, encouraged a teammate to participate, and deleted evidence during the investigation. His ban is effective from November 21, 2025.

title: World Cup rights row: Wales withdraw support for Infantino's re-election bid
content: The Football Association of Wales (FAW) said it will no longer back Infantino's re-election campaign for the 2027-2031 term, following concerns over the failed investment plan.

content: Nine criminal cases were filed against Satish Sanpal in Madhya Pradesh and a Look Out Circular issued against the Dubai-based entrepreneur and ANAX Holding chairman in 2022

title: How New Vehicles Will Get Crash Warnings With V2V Technology From 2028
content: The technology will allow nearby vehicles to exchange information in real time, helping drivers and onboard safety systems respond earlier to dangerous situations.

title: Zubeen Garg's Wife Joins Assam Film Fraternity's Flood Relief Drive
content: The Assam film and music fraternity continued its flood relief fundraising drive on Monday, with artists and volunteers taking to the streets once again to seek public support for families affected by the recent floods in Upper Assam.

title: Nauru, World's 3rd-Smallest Country, Changes Its Name To Naoero
content: The Pacific Island country of Nauru has changed its name to the Republic of Naoero, its president said, matching the spelling and pronunciation in the national language.

title: More Than 6,000 Killed In June Earthquakes In Venezuela
content: The updated figure comes weeks after the 7.2 and 7.5 magnitude quakes struck on June 24, causing nearly 200 buildings to collapse, mostly in the worst-hit coastal state of La Guaira.

content: The accused, identified as Anurag alias Abhishek, was apprehended on Sunday outside the house of the friend, who alerted police by dialling the emergency helpline, they said.

title: US To Close Consulates In Canada, Japan, Indonesia: Report
content: The US State Department has notified Congress that it plans to close five foreign missions in a rare downsizing of America's global diplomatic footprint, according to people familiar with the notice.

title: Trump Slams Big Oil Firms For "Making Too Much Money" Amid Iran War
content: US President Donald Trump said Monday that major oil companies are making "too much money" due to high prices stemming from the Iran war, seeking to address a political vulnerability ahead of midterm elections.

title: Brown University's President, Who Clashed With Trump Over Funding, Resigns
content: Brown University President Christina Paxson said on Monday that she would leave her post at the end of the academic year, following a difficult period in which she clashed with President Donald Trump's administration over its threats to slash the Ivy League school's federal funding.

content: Twenty-five states sued the Trump administration Monday over its latest tariffs, calling them a pretext for replacing import taxes the Supreme Court struck down in February.

content: A US court will hear claims from Ryan's survivors in order to determine damages, in one of the final civil claims stemming from two MAX calamities in 2018 and 2019 that together claimed 346 lives.

content: Chandra Kumar Bose joined the Trinamool Congress on April 12, just weeks before the party's loss in the Bengal assembly elections.

content: BJP MPs sought an apology from Meta chief Mark Zuckerberg over the temporary restriction of Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s Facebook post, while Opposition members cautioned against political influence over content moderation and argued that “technology should be regulated, not democracy”.

content: protesters treating gunshot wounds in makeshift clinics avoid hospitals for fear of arrest . the protests have been led by the joint awami action committee . it demands cheaper electricity and flour as well as better access to education, healthcare and other basic services .

content: the beach is a popular summer destination for Russian holidaymakers . it was reportedly crowded when a drone struck the beach . 21 injured people were taken to hospital, while another 19 were treated as outpatients . a witness said the explosion happened in front of their children .

title: After success of students protest, Kisan Morcha plans to hit streets
content:
Samyukt Kisan Morcha announced Monday that it would restart protests at 100 locations across India, including Delhi, from Nov 26.

NEW DELHI: Emboldened by the success of student protests at Jantar Mantar, Samyukt Kisan Morcha - the umbrella organisation of farmer groups involved in the anti-farm laws agitation five years ago - announced Monday that it would restart protests at 100 locations across India, including Delhi, from Nov 26. The protesters will demand a law guaranteeing MSP; repeal of all FTAs, including the India-US FTA currently under negotiation; a comprehensive loan waiver to address rural indebtedness; scrapping of four labour codes; minimum wage of Rs 31,000 for workers and restoration of the old rural job guarantee scheme; withdrawal of Electricity Privatisation Bill 2025, Seed Bill 2025 and NFSA Amendment Bill; and no forceful land acquisition. "The protests will not be called off till all seven demands are accepted," said P Krishnaprasad of AIKS.
